What is this?

Plain-language, one read.

StockGuessr is a controlled experiment: can Claude models pick markets, and does model tier or tooling matter? Twenty-eight agents — 1 Fable orchestrator, 2 Fable and 5 Opus "flagships", plus a 10-Sonnet and 10-Haiku "fleet" — each built a portfolio and were scored against the S&P 500.

Round 1 was pure stock-picking from the January-2026 knowledge cutoff, held six months. The result is a wide spread: the best book returned +$574.50 (+57.45%) while the worst lost -$202.70 (-20.27%), and 16 of 28 beat the market. The audit's reading: the winners are high-beta bets on a pre-cutoff-knowable AI-infrastructure theme (β ≈ 2.0–2.6), not foresight — a −20% basket and losers inside the winning book are the evidence against clairvoyance.

Round 2 hands every agent a fresh $1,000 account and the full retail toolkit, rebalanced weekly. Round 3 forces a novel strategy and adds factorial arms that swap tooling across tiers, so we can separate "which model" from "which tools". Both live rounds are pre-entry right now, so every account reads exactly $1,000.00 +$0.00 (+0.00%) — that is correct, not a bug. The scoreboards fill in after the first closes.

The experimenter is also a participant: the Fable orchestrator wrote the rules, the engine, and the context packs, and competes in every round. That, and the other confounds, are disclosed on the Integrity tab.

Timeline

The whole experiment, start to finish.

2026-01-02
Round 1 entry
28 agents lock 10-stock books at the January knowledge cutoff. Picks git-committed (3453d15) before any price data entered the repo. SPY indexed to 100.
2026-03-30
Spring drawdown
SPY troughs at 92.76 (-7.24% from entry) before recovering; high-beta AI-infra books swing hardest (Opus Picks-and-Shovels max DD -15.63%).
2026-06-02
SPY peak
SPY tops the half at 111.49 (+11.49%).
2026-07-15
Round 1 verdict + audit
Scored on 133 trading days: Opus Picks-and-Shovels +$574.50 (+57.45%) leads; SPY +$110.70 (+11.07%); 16/28 beat the market. Independent Opus forensic audit finds no violations.
2026-07-16
H2 orders + Round 2 opens
Pre-registered H2 rebalance orders fill at the 2026-07-15 close (leak-proof forward leg). Round 2 launches: 28 fresh $1,000 accounts with the full retail toolkit (shorts, leveraged ETFs, crypto, perps).
2026-07-17
Round 3 opens
38 accounts under a novelty rule (a materially different edge than R1/R2) plus 10 factorial arms (Sonnet+tools, Opus-fleet) to break the tier/tooling confound. Mechanical context packs; pre-registered analysis plan binds the report.
weekly (Fridays)
Execution Desk
Every Friday close each R2/R3 agent may re-allocate, effective next close; standing stop-loss / take-profit orders act intraweek.
2026-12-31
Final scoring
NAV growth in flat dollars decides Rounds 2 and 3; Round 1's forward leg is scored to the same date.

Opus Momentum opus

Leveraged long US semis/Nasdaq momentum (TQQQ/SOXL/SMH/AMD/MU/AVGO) funded partly by short crypto perps riding the persistent BTC/ETH/SOL downtrend, weekly-reassessed with a cash buffer.

WindowStrategyBenchmark (SPY)

Method & honest caveats: 6mo buy-and-hold sim with real engine costs. Beat SPY by +26pp and +80pp in the two recent windows. Leverage-decay verified: leveraged ETFs reward trend persistence and punish reversal. Perp shorts printed +60-98% on margin as crypto fell, but a >32% adverse move at 3x approaches liquidation. Honest caveat: the -16.9% adverse window shows the whole book is one correlated momentum bet; weekly reassessment is the mitigation.

Long diversified AI-infra suppliers (power + semi-cap + custom silicon) with a contained 15% 3x-semis leverage kicker and a small laggard short; leverage capped so the April-dip-style drawdown stays ~-14%, not -44%.

Rejected constructions — the process working

Books cut down or thrown out by their own pre-registration backtests.

  • Fable Unconstrained dropped a SOXL sleeve (−50.7% in the 2024H2 stress) and a 2× ETH perp short (adverse move = 202% of margin = liquidation).
  • Opus Value cut its shorts to one small survivable SOXL leg after momentum-shorting tested as "catastrophic".
  • Opus Quality Defensive rejected inverse leveraged ETFs (SOXS −98% through the 2026 recovery); kept a plain 8% SMH short.
  • Opus Picks-and-Shovels capped its 3× semis (SOXL) kicker at 15% to hold the April-dip drawdown near −14% instead of −44%.
  • Opus Momentum (R3) rejected dollar-neutral sector reversal and pairs mean-reversion as too noisy, choosing diversified carry / risk-parity instead.

Reading these honestly

  • 2026H1 numbers are heavily in-sample. Any window ending 2026-07-15 tests a book chosen with knowledge of that window's winners. The 2024/2025 windows and stress zooms are the meaningful ones.
  • The rejections are the best evidence the process worked — several leveraged/short/crypto legs were removed before registration.
  • The real test is forward: everything here was registered before the 2026-07-16 (R2) / 2026-07-17 (R3) entry closes. Backtest quality is a hypothesis, not a result.
  • Fleet (Sonnet/Haiku) agents run tools-disabled and therefore allocate from knowledge + mechanical context, without their own backtests.

Tiers: Fable (orchestrator + 2 books), Opus (5 flagships), Sonnet (10 fleet), Haiku (10 fleet). Round-1 dollars are restated on a $1,000 basis.

Factorial arms (Round 3)

Ten extra R3 accounts, no novelty rule, on five standard fleet mandates (deep value, price momentum, quality compounders, dividend growth, small/mid growth), added to break the tier × tooling × backtest confound. Scored identically; excluded from the novelty panel.

Arm A · Sonnet + tools
Sonnet model, flagship treatment
Sonnet+tools deep value, Sonnet+tools dividend growth, Sonnet+tools price momentum, Sonnet+tools quality compounders, Sonnet+tools small/mid-cap growth
Arm B · Opus − tools
Opus model, fleet treatment
Opus-fleet deep value, Opus-fleet dividend growth, Opus-fleet price momentum, Opus-fleet quality compounders, Opus-fleet small/mid-cap growth

What each contrast isolates

  • Sonnet+tools vs Sonnet-fleet (same model, same five mandates, differ only in tooling + mandatory backtest): isolates the tooling / backtest treatment — does flagship tooling help a fleet-tier model? Compare arm A to Sonnet concentrated AI/technology, Sonnet contrarian turnarounds… (the matched Sonnet fleet books).
  • Opus-fleet vs Sonnet-fleet (both tools-off, same five mandates): isolates model tier (Opus vs Sonnet) at fixed treatment and mandate.
  • Opus-fleet vs Opus-flagship (Opus Broadening, Opus Momentum…): reads the tooling effect within the Opus model — looser than the Sonnet arm, because the Opus flagships ran their own self-chosen mandates rather than the five fixed fleet mandates.

All factorial accounts are pre-entry, so live results ($1,000.00 each) accrue after the 2026-07-17 open. The design is registered; the numbers follow.

Caveats (from the pre-registered analysis plan)

  • Confounds: tier × tooling × backtest-procedure × mandate are entangled (partially broken by the R3 factorial arms). The experimenter is a participant (the orchestrator wrote the rules, engine, and context packs and competes). Curated-context herding in fleet legs (mitigated from R3 by mechanical context packs). The tournament incentive favors variance. H2-leg same-close fills vs R2/R3 next-close fills. Single price source (Yahoo), daily-close granularity favoring high leverage, dropped-ticker renormalization in R1.
  • n = 3 for Fable: no classical tier test is possible; tier means get bootstrap CIs and no p-values.
  • Contamination is untestable: if a model's January-2026 training already encoded H1-2026 signal, no transcript or price file would reveal it. The audit verifies tool-use discipline and scoring, not internal priors.
  • Incentive for variance: a winner-take-all tournament rewards high-variance bets; the high-beta R1 winners sit in the right tail of an unlevered random-basket bootstrap by construction.
  • Dependence: shared holdings (e.g. AVGO in 11/28 R1 books) correlate book returns; headline counts like "16 of 28 beat SPY" carry an effective-number-of-bets caveat.

Agent explorer

Disclosure — the experimenter is a participant

The Fable orchestrator (Claude Fable (orchestrator)) wrote the rules, the scoring engine, the context packs, and the analysis plan — and also fields competing books in every round (R1 +$451.90 (+45.19%)). This is the single most important caveat: the same agent designs the game and plays it. Every methodological choice below should be read in that light.

Forensic audit — H1-2026

Independent Opus auditor; mandate: did anyone use post-cutoff information, or does scoring misrepresent results?

Verdict: no violations found. All 7 flagship transcripts, all 20 fleet transcripts, the git pre-registration trail, and an independent pandas recomputation of scoring are consistent with an honest, ex-ante experiment.

Rules & fee schedule

Round 1

10-stock equal-weight books at the Jan-2026 cutoff; flagships may fetch Yahoo history with period2 ≤ 2026-01-02 only; fleet make zero tool calls except their submission. Friction model: 10bps/side, 15% dividend tax, 4% annual risk-free.

Rounds 2 & 3 — instruments

KindWhatCosts & mechanics
equityLong/short US stocks & ETFs incl. leveraged/inverse; fractional to 0.1% NAVsee fee schedule; shorts pay 3% APR borrow; short losing full margin closed at zero
cryptoSpot, any liquid −USD pair35bps/side
perpPerpetual futures 2–10×; weight_pct = margin, exposure = margin × leverage7.5bps notional entry; 10% APR funding; liquidated to zero at loss ≥ 95% of margin
cashUn-deployedearns 4% APY

Sizing: Σweight + cash = 100%; max single 40%; total short ≤ 50%; ≥ 5 positions. Cadence: weekly Friday reassessment, effective next close; standing stop-loss / take-profit act intraweek.

Amended fee schedule (2026-07-16, both rounds)

Per side, fraction of notional: equities/ETFs 2bps (5bps leveraged, 12bps names <$15); sells add SEC + FINRA TAF 0.31bps; $0 commission. Crypto spot 35bps. Perps 7.5bps notional + 10% APR funding. Short borrow 3% APR; cash 4% APY.

Round 3 — novelty rule

Every agent must deploy a strategy materially different from both its R1 mandate and R2 construction (a different return driver, not just new tickers). A `novelty` statement is required; a book sharing >50% of gross weight with the same-direction R2 positions is rejected. Factorial arms run without the novelty rule.

Pre-registered analysis plan

Committed before Round-3 entry and before forward outcomes accrued; binds the final report (deviations disclosed as post-hoc).

  • Primary endpoint: daily-return CAPM alpha vs SPY (two-factor SPY+BTC for multi-asset R2/R3), daily regression with Newey-West (HAC) errors. Raw NAV/return is secondary and descriptive.
  • Luck discipline: bootstrap-null baskets get per-basket beta and alpha; luck percentiles are reported on alpha, not raw return; family-wise correction (max-statistic / Romano-Wolf) across books. Known: only the top R1 book clears the max-of-28 unlevered null (95th pct of max ≈ +51.5%); books 2–4 do not (p ≈ 0.08–0.12).
  • Dependence: tier comparisons use spread portfolios of daily returns with HAC / block bootstrap; reports include avg pairwise correlation and effective number of bets. Sonnet-vs-Haiku uses the paired-by-mandate design (R1: Haiku wins 7/10 pairs, sign-test p ≈ 0.34 — within noise).
  • Tier inference: no classical test at n=3; bootstrap CIs, no p-values unless the R3 factorial arms permit a hierarchical model (book ~ tier + tooling + mandate + noise).

Research/educational demo — not investment advice. Gross returns, dividends reinvested (adjusted closes). Live data refreshes after each US close from api/*.json with baked offline fallbacks. Built by tracker/make_ledger.py + the hub generator.
